title: The 1965–1966 Indonesian Mass Killings and CIA Involvement
summary: The systematic anti-communist purge and extermination of between 500,000 and 1,000,000+ suspected leftists, trade unionists, peasant organizers, and ethnic Chinese in Indonesia, orchestrated by the Indonesian military under Major General Suharto with covert financial, logistical, and intelligence assistance from the United States government and the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA). Declassified diplomatic cables confirmed that US Embassy officials compiled and provided comprehensive execution lists containing thousands of names of Communist Party of Indonesia (PKI) leaders and members to Indonesian army death squads, while US radio equipment and covert funds facilitated nationwide extermination operations.
background: During the early 1960s, Indonesia was led by its founding anti-colonial President Sukarno, an architect of the Non-Aligned Movement who adopted increasingly anti-imperialist policies, expropriated Western corporate holdings, and maintained a governing coalition with the Communist Party of Indonesia (PKI)—the third largest communist party globally with over 3 million members. Washington viewed Sukarno with extreme hostility. On the night of September 30, 1965, an internal military faction calling itself the September 30th Movement kidnapped and executed six senior right-wing army generals. Major General Suharto rapidly mobilized loyalist units, suppressed the movement, and falsely accused the PKI leadership of orchestrating a nationwide communist coup. The military and allied religious and youth militias (such as Ansor and Pemuda Pancasila) launched a nationwide campaign of mass extermination.

chronology.headline: Suharto Takes Command of Army
chronology.detail: Major General Suharto assumes emergency control of the armed forces, establishing the operational command Kopkamtib and launching coordinated radio propaganda blaming the PKI for the assassination of six generals.

chronology.headline: US Embassy Pledges Covert Assistance
chronology.detail: US Ambassador Marshall Green cables the State Department urging full support for the military: 'The army is our best hope... we should indicate our covert support to the extent we can.' The CIA delivers secure tactical communication gear to Suharto's headquarters.

chronology.headline: US Intelligence Compiles and Transfers Kill Lists
chronology.detail: Political officer Robert J. Martens and CIA officers at the US Embassy systematically compile detailed dossiers and name lists of thousands of regional and national PKI leaders, hand-delivering them to Suharto's senior aides to be 'ticked off' as they were captured and murdered.

chronology.headline: Peak of Mass Executions Across Java and Bali
chronology.detail: Military death squads and paramilitary groups slaughter tens of thousands nightly. Rivers across Central Java and Bali are choked with decapitated bodies; entire villages suspected of leftist sympathies are liquidated.

chronology.headline: Supersemar Transfer of Executive Power
chronology.detail: Suharto forces a weakened President Sukarno to sign the 'Supersemar' decree transferring executive governing authority to the military, banning the PKI, and arresting cabinet ministers.

chronology.headline: Freeport Mining Concession Signed
chronology.detail: Suharto enacts Foreign Investment Law No. 1, awarding US mining firm Freeport Sulphur an exclusive multi-decade concession to the Grasberg gold and copper reserves in West Papua.

documented_consequences.political: Total annihilation of the Indonesian left and progressive trade union movement; establishment of Suharto's 32-year brutal military dictatorship (the 'New Order'); integration of Indonesia into the Western geopolitical and commercial sphere.
documented_consequences.civilian_toll: Rigorous historical inquiries (including the 2012 Indonesian Komnas HAM Judicial Report and declassified US archives) document that between 500,000 and 1,000,000+ civilians were systematically murdered without trial, with bodies buried in mass graves or dumped into rivers. An additional 1,000,000 to 1,500,000 people were interned in concentration camps under forced labor, with civil rights stripped from their families for decades.
documented_consequences.long_term: The 'Jakarta Method' became the recognized operational blueprint for US-backed extermination of left-wing democratic movements globally, directly inspiring Operation Condor in South America and counter-insurgency death squads in Central America.

disputed_aspects: Exact overall death toll figures: Academic estimates range from 500,000 (conservative census differential analysis by Robert Cribb) to over 1.2 million (Indonesian military commander Sarwo Edhie Wibowo's deathbed estimate and Komnas HAM projections).
The internal origins of the September 30th Movement: Whether it was an authentic mutiny of junior nationalist officers acting independently or manipulated by intelligence provocateurs.
